newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends lower on weather, cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends lower on weather, cash.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures ended mostly lower Wednesday as mild weather forecasts put downward pressure on cash and traders covered shorts ahead of the storage data.
May finished 1.5 cents lower at $1.867 but still held the $1.85 support level. June settled down 1.7 cents at $1.927, while other deferreds remained flat to lower at the close.

"It's out of winter mode but not yet in spring mode. The market is just idling," one source said, adding most speculative buyers are remaining on the sidelines until clearer signs on the market's direction emerge.

In ACCESS, May was 0.7 cent lower at $1.86 at 1610 EST following the release of American Gas Association storage data, showing a drop of only one bcf to 26 percent of capacity, or 257 bcf ahead of a year ago.
The 28 bcf drop in the Consuming Region East was counteracted by a 24 bcf build seen in the Producing Region. In the West, three bcf of gas was withdrawn last week.
Support in May was still pegged at $1.825, $1.78 and the contract low of $1.71. Traders said resistance was still at $1.95-1.97, and then at $2.04-2.05.
NYMEX's 12-month strip fell a half cent to $2.082 as an estimated 22,393 Hub contracts traded. Open interest for April 1 gained another 1,295 lots to 166,331.

In the cash market, U.S. Gulf Coast prices remained close to futures in the low-to-mid $1.80s, erasing Tuesday's 10-cent gain. Henry Hub was quoted mostly at $1.84-1.86. Prices on the Midcontinent pipes eased by about three cents to $1.72-1.75, while New York city-gate values were steady at $2.18-2.20.

Temperatures throughout the U.S. are expected to remain normal to above normal through the weekend, except in the Southwest where temperatures are forecast to hover about five to 10 degrees below normal, Weather Services Corp.
No Permian or Alberta natgas futures traded.
On KCBT, May settled one cent lower at $1.73, while deferreds were flat to a half-cent higher. The East/West spread widened by 0.2 cent to 13.7 cents (NYMEX premium).
Physical prices in the Permian basin were even with futures in the low-to-mid $1.70s, down about three cents from Tuesday.
